source_context: \uline{Lemme} Soit $\unsure{\gamma|\Gamma}$ un groupe, opérant de façon transitive sur un ens. $J$, et considérons un sous-schéma $\mathcal X$ de $X_J$ \inserted{(où $X=\operatorname{Spec}k$)} qui soit tel que
b) le composé $k\longrightarrow\Gamma(\unsure{X_J},\mathcal O_{\unsure{X_J}})$ $(\simeq k^J)$ est injectif.
il correspond à un sous-schéma fermé de $X$ donc à un idéal $\unsure{\mathfrak a}$ de $k$.
rows.what_the_ink_shows: The lemma's statement reads 'un sous-schéma' followed by the calligraphic X and 'de X_J'; there is no 'fermé' in that hypothesis or an insertion adding it. The inserted parenthesis identifies X as Spec k (crops/84_scan120_L47_L1230_subscheme_hypothesis.jpg). In condition b, the argument of Gamma is visibly X with a J subscript, and the structure-sheaf subscript likewise reads X_J. The adjacent parenthesis is approximately-equal k to the power J, followed by 'est injectif' (crops/84_scan120_L47_L1230_injectivity_hypothesis.jpg). Later in the proof, 'sous-schéma fermé de X' is explicitly written; that occurrence does not appear in the lemma's hypothesis (crops/84_scan120_L47_L1230_proof_closed_subscheme.jpg).
rows.note: Preserve the lemma's unqualified 'sous-schéma' and the written map into Gamma(X_J,O_X_J). Replacing its domain of sections by the subscheme and adding 'fermé' to the hypothesis would repair the proposed mathematics rather than recover omitted or misread ink. The source already records 'fermé' where it occurs in the proof. Preserve all existing uncertainty macros and other text. The earlier lemma-hypothesis report, counterexample, and SA02-R84-14 recheck are background only; none was independently re-proved in this visual inspection.
